title: Lower-moment norm equivalence for renewal partial sums
statement:
Let $(X_k)$ be independent copies of a nondegenerate nonnegative random variable, let $S_n=X_1+\cdots+X_n$, and set $Z_n=\sum_{k=1}^n e^{\imath S_k}$. For $p>0$, write $\|Z_n\|_p=(\mathbb E|Z_n|^p)^{1/p}$. **Renewal-sum norm conjecture.** One has

$$
\|Z_n\|_p\asymp \|Z_n\|_2
$$

for $p<2$. The preceding argument establishes the analogous equivalence for $p\geq 2$, while the lower-moment range is left as a conjectural extension.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.05574

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2025).
source_name: Jerzy Szulga, “Improper Poisson integral of the sinc function”, arXiv:2504.05574 (2025).

progress.label: Open · solution reported
progress.tldr: A posted argument claims to prove the conjecture in all cases, but no independent source has checked it, so the problem is not verified as solved.
progress.summary:
Szulga's 2025 paper studies renewal-point-process sums and indicates that broader questions are left as conjectures; it does not verify this norm equivalence.

*[arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.05574)*

**Posted attempt**

An unverified argument claims a complete proof: it interpolates between the known fourth-moment bound and the target lower moment when $|\mathbb{E}e^{\imath X_1}|<1$, and treats the boundary case $|\mathbb{E}e^{\imath X_1}|=1$ as deterministic. The argument has not been independently verified.

Current status (as of August 2026): A complete proof has been posted but remains unverified; no corroborated resolution of the lower-moment conjecture is recorded.

*Caveats. The claimed proof depends on the stated fourth-moment estimate and its applicability to the full hypothesis, neither of which is independently documented in the retrieved discussion.*

solutions.body:
The conjecture follows from the fourth-moment estimate already proved in Lemma 2.1.1(3).

Let
\[
S_k=X_1+\cdots+X_k,
\qquad
Z_n=\sum_{k=1}^n e^{iS_k},
\]
and first assume the source hypothesis
\[
r=\left|\mathbb E e^{iX_1}\right|<1.
\]
The cited lemma supplies a constant \(C_4\ge1\), independent of \(n\), such that
\[
\|Z_n\|_4\le C_4\|Z_n\|_2.
\]

Fix any \(0<p<2\), and set
\[
\theta=\frac{p}{4-p},
\qquad
\frac12=\frac{\theta}{p}+\frac{1-\theta}{4}.
\]
Log-convexity of moments gives
\[
\|Z_n\|_2
\le\|Z_n\|_p^\theta\|Z_n\|_4^{1-\theta}
\le C_4^{1-\theta}
\|Z_n\|_p^\theta\|Z_n\|_2^{1-\theta}.
\]
This interpolation inequality follows directly from Hölder's inequality and remains valid even when \(0<p<1\). If \(\|Z_n\|_2>0\), rearrangement yields
\[
C_4^{-(4-2p)/p}\|Z_n\|_2
\le\|Z_n\|_p
\le\|Z_n\|_2,
\]
where the upper bound is monotonicity of moments on a probability space. If \(\|Z_n\|_2=0\), both sides vanish. Hence
\[
\|Z_n\|_p\asymp\|Z_n\|_2
\qquad(0<p<2)
\]
uniformly in \(n\).

The boundary case omitted by the source hypothesis is also immediate. If \(r=1\), equality for the expectation of the unit-modulus random variable \(e^{iX_1}\) implies
\[
e^{iX_1}=\lambda\quad\text{almost surely}
\]
for some \(|\lambda|=1\). Thus
\[
Z_n=\sum_{k=1}^n\lambda^k
\]
is deterministic, and \(\|Z_n\|_p=\|Z_n\|_2\) for every \(p>0\). Therefore the requested equivalence holds for every increment distribution, including the lattice boundary case.
